title: Enterprise security questionnaire triggers: billing hold + temporary escrow credit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When an enterprise customer submits a security questionnaire that uncovers a potential compliance blocker (data residency, encryption gaps, or high-risk network configuration), Sales and Solutions Engineering often request a temporary billing hold or escrow-style credit for pending remediation. This ticket defines the product flow, ledger model, API surface, and UI to support a secure, auditable 'security-questionnaire hold' that: creates a temporary refundable credit/escrow line on the account, pauses automated invoice generation for affected billing lines, preserves usage metering for analytics, and provides manual overrides and reconciliations for account teams.
background: Recent enterprise deals delayed by security questionnaire findings have required manual finance coordination: one-off credits, invoice voids, and ad-hoc refunds. This creates operational overhead, invoice confusion, and audit risk. We need a structured, auditable product flow so legal/sales can offer consistent remediation credits without breaking metering invariants or SLAs for other customers.
scope: In scope: - Add a 'security_questionnaire_hold' billing state on accounts/subscriptions. - Ledger entries for temporary escrow credit lines tagged to a questionnaire case ID. - API endpoints for creating/releasing holds and for Finance to apply manual reconciliations. - Console UX for PMs/AMs to see hold state, reason, case links, and to release/adjust. - Audit log entries with links to questionnaire artifacts and support tickets. - Autos-release policy and notification templates.
out_of_scope: Out of scope: - Automated remediation actions that change infra or compliance posture. - Changes to core reservation/commit pricing model beyond tagging. - Cross-account consolidated invoices (handled by separate billing consolidation project).
ledger_model: Design: temporary escrow credit is a refundable negative charge line with metadata: {case_id, created_by, hold_reason, max_refund_amount, expires_at}. The account balance excludes the escrow amount from collections while in hold. Upon release, we either: (a) convert escrow to invoice credit (applied to next invoice) or (b) issue a refund and close the case. All transitions produce immutable audit records. The escrow line must support partial refunds and memo fields for legal notes.
api_changes: New endpoints: POST /v1/accounts/{id}/holds to create hold; GET /v1/accounts/{id}/holds to list; PATCH /v1/holds/{hold_id} for status changes; POST /v1/holds/{hold_id}/release with {method: 'apply_credit'|'refund'|'void'}. Responses include ledger transaction IDs. Require role-based auth checks: only finance/solutions/sales roles can create holds. API errors documented for conflicts (existing hold on same invoice period).
ui_changes: Console: Account > Billing tab: show 'Holds & Escrow' panel with active holds, reason, case link, created_by, created_at, expires_at, and quick actions: 'Release -> Apply to next invoice', 'Release -> Refund', 'Extend hold'. Add modal to capture legal justification and attach questionnaire link. Keep existing invoice UI intact but annotate invoices that were paused due to an active hold.
edge_cases: Multiple concurrent holds on same account spanning overlapping invoice periods: policy => earliest-created hold takes precedence for pausing collections on a given invoice line; subsequent holds create separate escrow entries but do not retroactively pause already-paused invoices.
Reserved capacity + hold: reserved commitment charges continue to accrue; holds only affect metered/overage lines unless contract specifically references committed offsets.

Customer upgrades/downgrades mid-hold: usage continues to be metered; escrow applies only to billed items identified at the time of hold creation unless Finance selects 'recompute and apply to final usage'.

Expired hold with open remediation: system auto-notifies account team 7 days before expiration; after expiration, hold auto-escapes to a 'pending_review' state and requires manual action within 14 days or it will default to 'apply_credit' and generate invoice adjustments.
Chargeback and tax implications: credits applied must preserve tax calculation provenance; Finance must run tax re-calculation on release where relevant.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Alpha): 3 pilot enterprise accounts (Sales-approved) + internal finance users. Monitor: number of manual adjustments, time-to-release, customer confusion tickets. Phase 2 (Beta): expand to >20 accounts, add automated notification flows and account manager training. Phase 3 (GA): open to all enterprise accounts, add default autos-release policies and public docs. Rollout timeline: Alpha by 2025-03-15, Beta by 2025-03-31, GA by 2025-04-15.
acceptance_criteria: Create hold via API and Console: ledger entry created and invoice generation suppressed for targeted billing lines.
Release flow supports apply_credit, refund, and void; each produces correct ledger transactions and tax recalculation where applicable.
Audit trail preserved for every state transition with linkable questionnaire artifact and support ticket.
Finance manual override UI works and respects RBAC restrictions.
Pilot accounts report reduced manual billing operations and fewer invoice-related legal escalations (measure via pilot feedback).
